name: RNA-seq alignment and gene counts
description: Align RNA-seq reads to a genome with HISAT2 and count the reads per gene, ready for differential expression.
details: Use this when you have a reference genome and a gene annotation and want a table of read counts per gene, for example as input to DESeq2 or edgeR. The pipeline trims the reads with fastp, builds a HISAT2 index from your genome, aligns the reads (HISAT2 handles reads that span introns), sorts and indexes the alignments with samtools, counts reads per gene with featureCounts, and gathers everything into a MultiQC report. HISAT2 was chosen because it runs everywhere with modest memory. If you prefer STAR, build its index with the STAR genome generate step and swap the aligner by hand; the rest of the pipeline stays the same. The setup step asks how your library was made (its strandedness), because a wrong choice loses most reads. The genome index is built again on every run, which takes a few minutes for a large genome; this template suits small to medium genomes best. One single-end sample at a time.

inputs.label: Sequencing reads
inputs.hint: One FASTQ file of single-end RNA-seq reads, plain or compressed (.fastq or .fastq.gz).

inputs.label: Genome sequence
inputs.hint: The genome of your organism as a FASTA file.

inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.hint: The matching gene annotation in GTF format (exons with a gene_id).

settings.label: Library strandedness
settings.hint: Pick what your library kit makes. Most stranded Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. A wrong choice loses most reads; if unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment on the alignments first.

outputs.label: Gene counts
outputs.hint: One row per gene with the number of reads counted.

outputs.label: Sorted alignments
outputs.hint: The aligned reads (BAM), open with a genome browser.

outputs.label: Alignment index
outputs.hint: The .bai file next to the BAM.

references.label: Kim D, Paggi JM, Park C, Bennett C, Salzberg SL. Graph-based genome alignment and genotyping with HISAT2 and HISAT-genotype. Nature Biotechnology 2019;37:907-915.
